name: The Jackals of the South Marches

system.docHtml:
The Jackals of the South Marches

Overview

The Jackals are the most feared free company of the South Marches, the dry borderlands south of the [[doc-mtrrchybth|Matriarchy of Bethûa]] where the matriarchal writ grows thin. They are not a clan and not a marcher tribe but something stranger: a warband of the Houseless, gathered out of everything the great matriarchy to the north throws away. They take their name from their queen, the renegade spear-sister [[character-yasurajckl|Yâsûra the Jackal]] — an exiled Bethûan officer who built, out of the realm's castoffs, the one thing Bethûa fears above all others: a company of armed exiles, women and gelded men both, who know the matriarchy's own ways of war and owe it nothing.

This makes the Jackals an anomaly in their own country. The peoples of the South Marches are not matriarchal — they are pastoral nomad clans led by men, who pay Bethûa tribute, keep their own customs, and regard the rich realm on their northern horizon with wary hostility. A female-led warband would be unthinkable among the marcher clans themselves; the Jackals are tolerated, hired, and given room only because they are useful against a shared northern enemy, and because their queen has made them too dangerous to move against lightly.

Composition

Every Jackal of the true band is Houseless — by exile, by disgrace, or by the knife. They fall into three uneven parts:

  • The exiled women. The body of the band: Bethûan women cast out of the matriarchy — disgraced officers, ruined daughters of lesser clans, widows stripped of standing, women sold or fled. Many were trained in arms as all free Bethûan women are, and they bring the [[doc-mtrrchybth|realm's]] martial discipline south with them.
  • The Spádai core. The band's hard, disciplined heart: cast-out Spádai, the gelded eunuch-warriors who are the only men Bethûa ever trusts with steel. Houseless and heirless by their very nature even in honour, an exiled Spáda has less to lose than anyone alive — and these few fight in the trained Bethûan manner that makes the Jackals far more than a raider rabble.
  • The marcher men. The expendable mass: herders' sons and marcher raiders of the southern clans, hired and spent as light horse and front-rank fodder. They ride for loot, not for Yâsûra, and they are the first the band burns through and the first to scatter when plunder runs short. They are not of the Houseless brotherhood and know it.

Leadership

The Jackals are [[character-yasurajckl|Yâsûra the Jackal's]] creation and hers alone. There is no council and no succession — the band is held together by the warlord's will, her reputation, her years of Lonkha command, and the steady flow of loot and purpose she provides. Beneath her, her most trusted Spádai and exile-women serve as lieutenants and lead the riding-parties, but every one of them holds her place at Yâsûra's sufferance. The band's great strength and its great weakness are the same fact: it is an extension of one ruined, disciplined woman. Yâsûra's training and cunning make the Jackals formidable; her one consuming grudge — against the thief-taker [[character-zahirmlkht|Zahira Malkhet]], who engineered her exile — can drive the whole pack past the bounds of sense.

Territory

Primary: The South Marches — the drylands and pastoral borderlands south of [[doc-mtrrchybth|Bethûa's]] settled frontier, country Bethûa claims on its maps but does not truly hold.

Range: The Jackals ride well beyond their home country when a contract or a feud warrants, raiding into the southern cantons and, for the right price, taking work along the [[doc-midhalnrgn|Mídhalión Region]] coast and the shores of the [[doc-vylarianse|Vylarian Sea]]. Away from the marches and the saddle, however, much of their advantage falls away.

Operations

Raiding: Mounted, fast, and at home in waterless country, the Jackals strike the herds, caravans, and exposed villages of the frontier — Bethûan targets by preference — and are gone before a House levy can muster.

Hired blades: The band sells deniable violence — escort and protection, muscle for border feuds, and contract killings and ambushes for patrons who want a thing done where no Dómissa's writ runs. Because the Jackals answer to no House and no marcher clan, employing them keeps a patron's own hands clean.

Brokered grudges: Yâsûra's most exploitable trait is that she can be hired to do what she already means to do. A patron who knows the warlord's hatreds can set the pack on a chosen target for a fraction of its worth, letting her own grievance supply the ferocity. It is exactly this lever that [[character-casiaveric|Cassia Verric's]] Vylarian agents have pulled, paying through cut-outs to set the Jackals on [[character-zahirmlkht|Zahira Malkhet]] — a contract Yâsûra took as much for the oldest debt she owns as for coin.

Reputation and Relations

To Bethûa the Jackals are a peculiar horror: not mere bandits but the matriarchy's own exiles turned against it, armed women and gelded men who carry the realm's training into the lawless south. The Court of the Veil would rather see them destroyed than admit how they came to be. To the marcher clans they are useful and unsettling in equal measure — a hard blade to hire against the hated north, but a Houseless, woman-led thing that fits nowhere in marcher custom and is trusted by no one. To outside powers like Vylaria they are simply the best deniable muscle on the southern shore: blades that can be set against Bethûa without the hand behind them ever being seen.

The band's loyalty runs only as deep as its make-up. The Houseless core — the exile-women and the Spádai — are bound to Yâsûra by shared ruin and have nowhere else to go; they would die for her, because she is the only home left to them. The hired marcher men are another matter, and would scatter back into the clans the moment the warlord fell or the loot dried up.

A Prize Crosses the Marches

For all their standing as raiders and hired blades, the Jackals have lately become a piece in a far larger game than they bargained for. The fugitive Grammatíssa [[character-rshrhssfrn|Rashîra of House Safîrôn]] is crossing the Marches with the stolen Purple Warrant — incontrovertible proof of the matriarchy's corruption, sought by Bethûa to burn, by Vylaria to wield, and by [[doc-empirtkhpr|Ta'Kheperu]] to answer. Vylaria's coin, through [[character-casiaveric|Cassia Verric's]] cut-outs, hired the band only to delay the Hound, [[character-zahirmlkht|Zahira]] — but the Jackals rule the one road that prize must travel, and every faction now knows it. Whoever secures the register could buy the band outright or see it destroyed; and the Jackals, who answer to no one and whose queen has her own bitter score to settle with the realm the register condemns, are the wildcard that every power in the affair must reckon with and none can trust.

Identifying Marks

The Jackals keep no uniform and fly no banner — they are exiles and raiders, not a House guard. They are known instead by their manner of war: fast mounted bands striking from the open marches, the disciplined Bethûan fighting of their Spádai core amid the looser marcher horse, and a reputation cultivated to make victims yield before a blow is struck. Among themselves the Houseless are known by deed and by Yâsûra's favour rather than by any clan-name — for the surrendering of one's House, willing or forced, is the price of joining, and the only birthright a Jackal is permitted is the one the band earns at the warlord's side.
